title: Trump's Mystery 1.7% Inflation Number... Explained With Squirrels
summary: Explainer debunking Trump's 1.7% inflation figure against the 3.7% September CPI: gasoline drove the jump, core and shelter rose too, real pay has fallen six months running, and the 19% Biden figure is invented.

verdicts.note: The three monthly CPI changes to September 2026 sum to 1.1%, about 3.3% annualized, and the year-on-year rate was 3.7%.

Seasonally adjusted CPI-U rose from 332.568 in June to 336.298 in September 2026 (+1.1% in three months, about 4.6% annualized), far above 2%; the claim held only for the June-August window (May 333.979 to August 334.131, about 0.2% annualized) because of June's energy-driven -0.4% month.

assertions.quote: The price of gasoline jumped 9.1% in September alone. That one item was more than half of the whole month's increase.

verdicts.note: BLS reports the gasoline index rose 9.1% in September 2026 and accounted for over half of the 0.6% monthly all-items increase; over 12 months energy rose 20.4% due in large part to gasoline rising 34.2%.

assertions.quote: about 61% of everything in the basket is up more than 3% from a year ago. So, it's not one bad acorn.

verdicts.note: In September 2026 most major indexes rose (recreation, used cars, education, airline fares, medical care, apparel) and only a small number such as communication fell, and core CPI edged up to 2.6% from 2.4%; but core goods were up only 0.7% over the year and the core monthly rate was unchanged at 0.3%, so the broadening is modest rather than most categories accelerating.

assertions.quote: September was the sixth month in a row that pay lost the race to prices.
Shelter costs are up 3.2% over the year. Rent ticked up another 0.2 in September.

verdicts.note: Shelter rose 3.2% year on year against core CPI of 2.6% in September 2026.
Shelter rose 3.2% over the 12 months to September 2026 versus 2.6% for all items less food and energy, and 0.4% versus 0.3% on the month.

assertions.quote: Prices rose about 21% over Biden's 4 years. In the head nut's first 20 months this term, about 5.4.

verdicts.note: CPI rose about 21% over 2021-24 versus about 5% in the first 20 months of 2025-26, a slower pace as well as a shorter span.

CPI-U rose 21.4% from January 2021 to January 2025 (261.582 to 317.671) and 6.1% from January 2025 to September 2026 (to 336.94); the cumulative figure is far smaller, but it covers 20 months versus 48, and annualized the pace is 3.6% versus 5.0%, a smaller gap.

assertions.quote: Under Biden, the price index never got near 19%. It peaked at 9.1 in June 2022.

verdicts.note: CPI inflation peaked at 9.1% in June 2022 and was 3.0% in January 2025.
The 12-month CPI-U change peaked at 9.1% in June 2022; no month in 2021-2024 exceeded that, and nothing approached twenty percent.

assertions.quote: They jumped 1.3% the biggest monthly jump since March 2022, more than double what economists expected.

verdicts.note: PPI rose 1.3% in September 2026, over 6% year on year, but producer prices pass through to CPI only partially and with lags.

Food at home changed -0.1%, 0.0% and -0.1% in July-September 2026 while energy rose 5.2% in September and gasoline accounted for over half the monthly all-items rise; grocery prices are still up 1.8% over 12 months, so flat-to-falling describes recent months, not the year.
